title: Rooms Info — payload
description: A member asks a room's host what it holds about the room: its tier, its current epoch, how long it keeps its records and when it last pruned them, the limits the host applies to its files, and how much of them the room and the member have used.

roomId.description: The room's identifier. The host verifies the presentation against credentials issued by this identifier, never against a member list of its own.

presentation.description: Must confer the `read` action at this room's scope.

roomId.description: The room this describes, echoed so a response cannot be mistaken for another room's.

retentionPolicy.description: Absent means `chained`, as everywhere in this family.

recordRetention.description: The room's record retention in force: which records `rooms/records/prune` may remove, by age. Absent means none — no record is eligible by age. Served to every member who may read the room, because a record is never to be removed under a rule its readers could not have read.

lastPrune.description: The room's latest record prune: when, how many, and the version it took. Absent when the room's records have never been pruned. A reader whose copy of the room was synchronised below `lastPrune.version` rebuilds it (`RecordPrune`).

signalDelay.description: Whether the host waits a randomised interval before sending this room's `rooms/changed` signals (`rooms/signal-delay/set`). Always present, because a member deciding what to write, or how to read a signal's timing, needs to know which is in force: `randomised` for a room that has never set one.

epoch.description: The room's current epoch as the host knows it: the one a record or file must be sealed under to be accepted now.

limits.description: The limits the host applies to this room, after any override for the room and capped by the host-wide ceiling. `member` here is the room's default per-member allowance; the presenter's own, which may differ, is under `usage.member.limits`.

member.description: The presenter's own use and allowance: charged to the subject at the root of the presented chain, so an agent sees its member's figures. Absent on a `private` room, where the host does not know which member is asking.

limits.description: The limits that apply to this member in this room: an override set for them by the host's administrators if there is one, else the room's per-member default.

maxRecordDocumentBytes.description: The largest `rooms/records/put` request document the host accepts for this room, in bytes, measured as `maxDocumentBytes` measures it: the serialized Trust Task document as received, `proof` and `presentation` included, no transport envelope. Never above the bound the newest `rooms/records/put` version the host serves declares (2,097,152 bytes at 0.6). A host whose own per-record limit is lower — a write above it refused with `rooms/records/put:recordTooLarge` — MUST state that limit here. Absent: the host applies no limit of its own, and the declared bound governs. A writer whose record would not fit carries its content as a file.

maxChunkSize.description: The largest `chunks.chunkSize`, in bytes, the host accepts for this room's proxied transfers (`rooms/blobs/upload/chunk`, `rooms/blobs/chunk`) at its own size, without refusing the chunk document or charging it to a stricter budget than the room's transfer budget. A producer cutting a blob for a proxied upload SHOULD choose a `chunkSize` no larger, so a file's segment size is `maxChunkSize - 16` at most. Absent: the host accepts every chunk size the transfer ceiling admits, 262,144 bytes, whose chunk document `rooms/blobs/upload/chunk/0.2` bounds at 360,448 bytes.
